reason: I want to build the pump first, and heart muscle should provide the walls that squeeze the chambers.
expectation: The heart muscle will fill the pumping walls slot, leaving the pump needing direction control and a rhythm.

alternatives.reason: Making blood also supports the circuit, but I chose to start with the pump.

effect: The muscular walls provide the force to push blood, so the pump still needs direction control.
reaction: The distinction between containing blood and generating pressure makes sense.
reason: I want to complete the chamber fittings; valves should control the direction of blood flow.
expectation: The valves will fill the direction-control slot and help prevent blood from flowing backward; the pump may still need pacemaker cells.

alternatives.reason: Blood is needed for the circuit, but I want to finish the pump first.

effect: The valves provide direction control by responding to pressure differences; the pump still needs a rhythm.
reaction: The explanation of how valves guide flow makes sense.
reason: I want to finish the pump, and pacemaker cells should provide its rhythm.
expectation: The pacemaker cells will establish a rhythm for the muscular chambers, producing a rhythmic pump.

effect: The beating heart completes the pump; I now need to assemble the filled returning circuit.
reaction: The heart starting its own rhythm is an interesting detail.
reason: I want to make blood to fill the circuit, so I will combine its listed components.
expectation: Plasma and red blood cells will form blood, though the model may simplify its other components.

effect: The blood can carry oxygen, so I need to assemble the vessel route next.
reaction: Connecting the liquid component with oxygen-carrying cells makes their different roles clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and connecting arteries to capillaries should start the circuit.
expectation: The arteries and capillary networks will form part of a vessel route; veins will probably be needed for the return.

effect: The arteries and capillaries provide an outward route and a place for exchange with tissues; the route still needs a return.
reaction: The distinction between moving blood and exchanging substances makes the capillaries' role clearer.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and veins should complete the return route.
expectation: Adding veins will make a returning vessel circuit that can later be filled with blood and connected to the heart.

effect: The veins complete a route back toward the heart; the connected circuit still needs blood.
reaction: Closing the route makes the circuit easier to picture.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and adding blood should fill the vessel circuit.
expectation: The blood will fill the connected vessels, completing the filled returning circuit; it may still need to be connected to the heart.

effect: The blood-filled circuit is complete, and the remaining goal is to connect it to the heart.
reaction: Filling the circuit makes the pump's role easier to picture.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and connecting the heart should let it move blood through the circuit.
expectation: The beating heart will pump blood through the connected vessels and back toward the heart.

effect: Connecting the heart and filled circuit completed circulation and showed how the pump and route work together to supply distant tissues.
reaction: It was satisfying to bring the separate parts together, though the final combination was predictable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting arteries to capillaries was most worthwhile because it explained why tissues need an exchange route, not just blood flowing past them.

leastWorthwhile.text: The sequence of connecting veins, filling the circuit, and adding the heart felt repetitive because each was the only offered combination.

surprise.text: I found it interesting that cells in the heart start its repeating electrical rhythm without a separate brain command for every beat.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the parts had clear roles, although compatible-partner guidance supplied the choices.

continue.text: I would be mildly interested in continuing to see how circulation supplies the working arm, although I would hope for more meaningful choices than the final sequence offered.
